headline: German AI company Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, an open-weight English-German model with a one-million-token context that governments can run on their own hardware.
score_reason: A real open-weight release from Europe's best-known AI lab with notable specs, but a mid-size model whose benchmark claims are vendor-run.
importance_line: Public bodies and regulated European companies get a free-to-download bilingual model they can run in-house without sending data to a US cloud, though all performance figures come from Aleph Alpha itself and no independent test has been reported.
summary: TestingCatalog reports that Aleph Alpha, the Heidelberg-based AI lab, has published Kolibri, a 78-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model (a design that activates only about 3.5 billion parameters per word to keep running costs down) with weights free on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 licence and a context window of up to one million tokens, launched on German Unity Day, 3 Oct 2026. Aleph Alpha says it matches models with four times as many active parameters on maths, coding and long-document tasks and was trained to decline answering when evidence is missing, but these are the company's own benchmark results.
notes: Benchmarks vendor-run; release confirmed by public weights.
